entries.text: Broad-spectrum sunscreen used every morning is the best-supported everyday step for protecting skin from UV. Apply enough to cover face and neck, and reapply every few hours when outdoors.
In dry air, applying a moisturiser to slightly damp skin helps hold water in. A simple moisturiser with glycerin or ceramides is usually enough; extra products are rarely needed.
In humid weather, a lightweight gel or fluid texture is often more comfortable. Cleansing gently once or twice a day is enough; over-washing can irritate.

A gentle evening cleanse removes dirt and sunscreen. Products cannot be promised to detox skin or make it pollution-proof. Antioxidant products are being researched but are not proven to protect against pollution in everyday use.
Fragrance is a common trigger of irritation for sensitive skin. Introduce one new product at a time, and patch test on a small area for a few days first.

Retinol and exfoliating acids can irritate, especially together, so many people use them on different nights and always use sunscreen. Retinoids are usually avoided in pregnancy unless a doctor advises.
Vitamin C is an antioxidant that can be useful but may sting, and it does not replace sunscreen.
A common order is cleanser, then lightweight products, then moisturiser, then sunscreen in the morning. A short routine you keep up beats a long one you skip.
Check whether a product you already own does the same job before buying another. Most people need a gentle cleanser, a moisturiser and a sunscreen.
See a dermatologist for skin that is painful, swollen, bleeding, blistering, rapidly spreading, or not improving after a few weeks.
